title: A Thorn for the Veil Again
premise: In the city of Vellamere, where the Purist Edicts outlawed magic fifteen years ago, temple scribe Rosalind Delacroix survives by selling watered-down charms and erasing her own past from every ledger she keeps. When a mute child arrives speaking the Old Tongue—the language of the vanished kingdom of Avelorn—Rosalind realizes the child carries a fragment of the last dragon-fire, the living memory of everything the Edicts burned. Hunted by the Inquisitor who once spared her, Rosalind must retrace her mother's heretical journey to the Threshold Door, the last exit from a country that officially no longer exists. She finds the door, but opening it demands a memory in trade: she gives up her recollection of her mother, letting the child inherit Avelorn's fire and freedom while Rosalind stays behind, unremembering and finally free of the debt she could never pay.
about_author: Dominic Whitlock is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloging confiscated grimoires before their institution quietly burned them. They write fantasy about people who survive by forgetting, and live in a coastal city that prefers its history unexamined.

chapters.title: The Ledger of Small Sins
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV. We meet her in the temple scriptorium, forging harmless charms and falsifying her own records to stay invisible under the Purist Edicts. A routine audit by Inquisitor Halloway nearly exposes her mother's name in an old registry. Emotional beat: the exhausting vigilance of a life built on erasure.

chapters.title: A Child at the Door
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV. On the eve of the Edicts' anniversary, a mud-splattered child appears at her lodging speaking the Old Tongue of Avelorn—a language Rosalind knows only from her mother's forbidden lullabies. The child clutches a coal that never cools. Emotional beat: dread and reluctant wonder as the past knocks literally at her door.

chapters.title: What the Edicts Burned
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV, with a flashback chapter to fifteen years earlier. We learn how her mother was taken, how Rosalind survived by denouncing her, and how the dragon-fires of Avelorn were smothered one hearth at a time. The child's coal is the last ember. Emotional beat: guilt resurfacing as inheritance.

chapters.title: The Inquisitor's Mercy
chapters.summary: Alternating POV: Rosalind and Inquisitor Halloway. Halloway, who spared Rosalind fifteen years ago for reasons he never explained, identifies the Old Tongue in a market incident and begins closing the net. Rosalind hides the child in the temple's dead-letter archive. Emotional beat: the terrible intimacy between hunter and the one he chose not to hunt.

chapters.title: The Dead-Letter Archive
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV. Among confiscated letters never delivered, she finds her mother's final correspondence, which names the Threshold Door and the price of passage: one true memory, freely given. The child begins speaking in Rosalind's own mother's voice in dreams. Emotional beat: hope discovered in the wreckage of confiscated lives.

chapters.title: Road Through the Ash Country
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV. She flees the city with the child, crossing the ash-fields where Avelorn stood, following landmarks only the Old Tongue can name. Halloway pursues with a warrant and a private obsession. The coal dims each night. Emotional beat: the road as pilgrimage and penance, urgency mounting as the fire gutters.

chapters.title: The Village That Forgot Itself
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV with the child's perspective interwoven. In a village of Edict collaborators who traded their memories for safety, Rosalind sees her own future: comfortable, hollow, unhaunted. The child heals a villager's withered orchard with the last of the coal's warmth. Emotional beat: the price of survival made visible and unbearable.

chapters.title: Halloway's Confession
chapters.summary: Halloway's POV. Cornered at a river crossing, Halloway reveals he was Avelorn-born, that he burned his own name to survive, and that he spared Rosalind because her mother once spared him. He offers a bargain: the child for Rosalind's freedom. Emotional beat: the antagonist revealed as a mirror—what Rosalind becomes if she chooses safety again.

chapters.title: The Threshold Door
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV. Climax. In the ruined heart of old Avelorn, Rosalind finds the Door standing in a field of living grass. Halloway arrives; the child, dying as the coal gutters, can only cross if a memory holds the Door open. Rosalind chooses to surrender her memory of her mother—the debt paid at last—and forces the Door wide as Halloway, weeping, finally stands aside. Emotional beat: sacrifice as the only honest payment.

chapters.title: A Thorn for the Veil
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV, epilogue. Back in Vellamere, Rosalind no longer remembers her mother, only a thorn of grief she cannot name. The child is gone through the Door; the coal's warmth lingers faintly in Rosalind's ledger margins, where words in the Old Tongue appear that she cannot read but copies anyway. Emotional beat: bittersweet resolution—survival's price paid, and something inherited anyway.
